newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lafarge no comment on Redland move.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge no comment on Redland move.

text.p: French building materials company Lafarge declined to say on Thursday whether it intended to buy a French aggregates subsidiary being sold by Redland Plc of Britain, due to depressed market conditions.
"No comment," a Lafarge spokesman said when asked if the French firm was looking to buy Granulats, the Redland unit.
He added however "Lafarge's general strategy is to strengthen its presence in mature markets through high added value products, such as plasterboard and special materials."
Its policy in developing emerging markets was to start with cement, he said.
Granulats has a book value of 310 million stg and employs 2,500 people.
Industry sources said Lafarge was among 50 or 60 companies approached in the last couple of weeks by an investment bank retained by Redland to find a buyer for Granulats.

Redland chief executive Robert Napier told Reuters in an interview, "Our aggregates business is for sale. We are in active discussions with a number of interested parties." He declined to give their country of origin.

Lafarge on March 12 reported 1996 net attributable profit down more than 12 percent at 1.85 billion francs but forecast a big improvement for 1997, based on an expected rise in sales of more than 10 percent.
